newsitem.title: GERMANY: German govt, opposition said still far off tax deal.
newsitem.headline: German govt, opposition said still far off tax deal.

text.p: Oskar Lafontaine, chairman of Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said on Monday little progress was made at a meeting with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition aimed at reaching a deal on tax reform.
"There was no narrowing of the gap between our two positions," Lafontaine told a news conference.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel said a six-strong group would meet again on Friday to try find a compromise on corporate tax changes.

But Lafontaine said another round of full negotiations would only make sense if the group that meets on Friday comes to concrete results about how best to cut Germany's notoriously high wage overheads.
Waigel has put together proposals to cut 30 billion marks in tax over the next two years. But Lafontaine said that the impact on the German budget was unclear.
